html:
Robert Schuman was a French statesman born in Luxembourg City in 1886. As French foreign minister he launched the plan that grew into the European Union.

He grew up a German citizen in Luxembourg and Lorraine and became French when Lorraine returned to France after 1918. Living on the border, he saw how coal and steel fed the wars between France and Germany.

On 9 May 1950 he proposed pooling French and German coal and steel under a shared authority. This became the European Coal and Steel Community of 1952, the seed of the Treaty of Rome and the European Union. 9 May is now Europe Day. Luxembourg, his birthplace, became a seat of the new institutions.
